items.quote: brought it back to his own city to mourn for him and bury him. Then he laid the body in his own tomb
items.contrast: The first destination is the prophet’s city, not the tomb where he subsequently lays the body.
items.reason: The sequence explicitly says that the prophet brings the body to his city before placing it in his tomb.

items.quote: you who are in the other two companies that normally go off Sabbath duty are all to guard the temple for the king
items.contrast: The two companies going off duty are assigned to guard the temple, while the three companies going on duty receive other specified posts.
items.reason: The quoted instruction directly assigns guarding the temple for the king to the two companies that normally go off Sabbath duty.

items.quote: A son named Josiah will be born to the house of David. On you he will sacrifice the priests of the high places who make offerings here
items.contrast: Josiah is the future actor who will kill the priests; Jeroboam is merely present when the prophecy is delivered.
items.reason: The pronoun “he” refers to the immediately named son, Josiah, and sacrificing the priests entails killing them.

items.quote: Should I give up my oil, by which both gods and humans are honored, to hold sway over the trees?
items.contrast: The refusal is based on the cost of giving up the olive tree’s honored oil, not on the trees’ later approach to the fig tree.
items.reason: The olive tree presents relinquishing its oil as the reason it will not take power over the trees.

items.quote: So his servant ran him through, and he died. When the Israelites saw that Abimelek was dead
items.contrast: Abimelek is the person killed, while the servant is the one who performs the killing.
items.reason: The servant runs the other man through, and the following sentence identifies the dead man as Abimelek.
